newsitem.title: LATVIA: BOURSE TO TOUGHEN OFFICIAL LIST RULES.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE TO TOUGHEN OFFICIAL LIST RULES.

text.p: The Riga stock exchange said on Friday it would toughen criteria for the official list stocks, including raising the minimum capital requirement to three million lats from the current one million lats.
"The volume of a company's stock in issue will have to be three million lats and 25 percent of it will have to be publicly traded," Uldis Cerps, the bourse president, told a news conference.
A profit for the previous financial year and reports prepared according to international accounting standards will also be made mandatory, Cerps said.
The rules will come into effect after approval by the securities market commission.
"We will grant a two-year period for the present official list stocks to come up to the mark," Cerps said.
Only one of the five stocks currently on the official list, confectionary maker Staburadze, falls short of the minimum capital requirement. Its capital stands at two million lats.
